title: MacNeal–Harder straight cantilever, regular hex8 mesh with incompatible modes
source: MacNeal and Harder, 'A proposed standard set of problems to test finite element accuracy', Finite Elements in Analysis and Design 1 (1985) 3–20: Fig. 4(a) (p. 7) geometry, material and mesh; Table 3 (p. 10) theoretical tip displacements

quantities.quantity: tip displacement along the load, extension
quantities.reason: MacNeal and Harder grade an element A within 2% of the theoretical value on this prescribed coarse mesh (p. 14)

quantities.quantity: tip displacement along the load, in-plane shear (width 0.2)
quantities.reason: MacNeal and Harder grade an element A within 2% of the theoretical value on this prescribed coarse mesh (p. 14)
quantities.known_failure: 0.978 of the theory, grade B: one hex8 with incompatible modes through the depth of the prescribed mesh (MacNeal–Harder's HEXA(8): 0.981, Table 8(a) p. 15); refined meshes converge (cantilever-hex8-incompatible)

quantities.quantity: tip displacement along the load, out-of-plane shear (depth 0.1)
quantities.reason: MacNeal and Harder grade an element A within 2% of the theoretical value on this prescribed coarse mesh (p. 14)
quantities.known_failure: 0.973 of the theory, grade B, as for in-plane shear (MacNeal–Harder's HEXA(8): 0.981)

quantities.quantity: tip rotation under a unit twisting moment
quantities.reason: MacNeal and Harder grade an element A within 2% of the theoretical value on this prescribed coarse mesh (p. 14); the moment reaches the end through a distributing coupling
quantities.known_failure: 0.892 of the theory, grade C: one element across the section cannot represent the torsion warping (MacNeal–Harder's HEXA(8): 0.910, HEX20: 0.904)
